harmfulComponents: Trace gold, silver & palladium in circuitry
Smartphone.healthEffects: A damaged or crushed lithium battery can leak, overheat, or catch fire. Lead exposure from informal dismantling is linked to nerve and kidney damage, and brominated flame retardants have been associated with hormonal disruption.
Smartphone.environmentalEffects: When dumped in landfills, batteries corrode and leach lithium, cobalt, and heavy metals into soil and groundwater. Circuit boards contain precious metals that are lost forever if not recovered through proper recycling.
Smartphone.properDisposalTip: Never puncture or burn the battery. Hand the phone to a certified e-waste collector — the precious metals inside are valuable enough that many recyclers pay or offer credits for them.

harmfulComponents: Mercury in some older backlit screens
Laptop.healthEffects: Informal recycling (open-air burning of cables, acid stripping of boards) exposes workers and nearby residents to lead, mercury, and toxic fumes, which are linked to respiratory illness and neurological damage, especially in children.
Laptop.environmentalEffects: Heavy metals from an improperly discarded laptop can contaminate soil and groundwater for decades. The aluminum, copper, and rare-earth elements inside are fully recyclable but are wasted when the device goes to landfill.
Laptop.properDisposalTip: Wipe your data first, then hand it to a verified recycler. Working laptops are often refurbished and reused, which avoids the environmental cost of manufacturing a new one entirely.

harmfulComponents: Lead & tin solder on circuit boards
Computing Device.healthEffects: Improper disassembly releases lead and other heavy metals as dust or fumes, which can cause long-term neurological and respiratory harm.
Computing Device.environmentalEffects: Circuit boards leach metals into soil and water if landfilled. Proper recycling recovers copper, aluminum, and gold that would otherwise be mined again at high environmental cost.
Computing Device.properDisposalTip: Hand the device over intact rather than dismantling it yourself — certified recyclers have the equipment to safely recover materials.

Monitor.healthEffects: A cracked CRT monitor can release lead dust; damaged mercury backlights release vapor that's toxic if inhaled. Both are linked to nervous system damage with prolonged exposure.
Monitor.environmentalEffects: Lead and mercury from broken monitors are persistent environmental contaminants — they don't break down and accumulate in soil, water, and the food chain.
Monitor.properDisposalTip: Never break the screen to make it 'smaller' for disposal. Transport it whole to a collection centre equipped to handle glass and mercury safely.

Battery / Power.healthEffects: Batteries are one of the most hazardous e-waste categories. Puncturing or crushing them can cause fires or chemical burns. Cadmium and lead exposure are linked to kidney damage and developmental harm in children.
Battery / Power.environmentalEffects: A single battery in a landfill can contaminate a large volume of soil and groundwater with heavy metals. This is why batteries are treated as hazardous waste in most regulations, not ordinary trash.
Battery / Power.properDisposalTip: Never throw batteries in regular household trash. Tape terminals if damaged, and take them to a dedicated battery drop-off or e-waste collector — this category typically carries the highest hazardous-material credit bonus.

Small Household Appliance.healthEffects: Burning PVC-coated wire (a common informal recycling shortcut) releases dioxins, which are carcinogenic and persist in the body for years.
Small Household Appliance.environmentalEffects: Plastic housings that aren't recycled break down into microplastics; internal metals leach into soil if landfilled.
Small Household Appliance.properDisposalTip: Keep it intact and hand it to a collector rather than stripping wires yourself — wire burning is illegal in most jurisdictions precisely because of the health risk.

harmfulComponents: Lead in older wiring and solder
Insulation foam blown with ozone-depleting gases
Large Household Appliance.healthEffects: Refrigerant gases don't directly poison people on contact, but improperly vented CFCs contribute to ozone depletion, which increases UV exposure and skin cancer risk population-wide.
Large Household Appliance.environmentalEffects: A single fridge's refrigerant, if vented instead of safely recovered, can have the greenhouse impact of driving a car for a year. Compressor oil is also a groundwater contaminant if it leaks.
Large Household Appliance.properDisposalTip: Never puncture the refrigerant lines. These appliances need a specialized recycler that can safely recover the refrigerant before the unit is scrapped.

harmfulComponents: Brominated flame retardants in plastic casings
Consumer Electronics.healthEffects: Fumes from burning plastic casings (common in informal scrap yards) are linked to respiratory irritation and long-term cancer risk.
Consumer Electronics.environmentalEffects: Untreated plastics and flame retardants persist in the environment and can bioaccumulate up the food chain.
Consumer Electronics.properDisposalTip: Hand devices to a verified collector rather than disposing of them with regular household waste.

harmfulComponents: Heavy metals such as lead, mercury or cadmium
default.healthEffects: Informal handling of electronic waste — burning, acid stripping, or manual disassembly without protection — exposes people to toxic metals and fumes linked to respiratory, neurological, and developmental harm.
default.environmentalEffects: Electronic waste sent to landfill leaches heavy metals and chemicals into soil and groundwater, and wastes recoverable materials like copper, aluminum, and precious metals.
default.properDisposalTip: Don't put this in regular household trash. Hand it to a verified collection centre or recycler so hazardous materials are handled safely and valuable materials are recovered.
